Exact finite-field enumeration across q=2,3,4,5,7,8,9,11 confirmed 136 fibers; finite checks only corroborative.

broader_coverage.reasoning: A theorem counting all nonzero determinants is a marginalization of, and strictly weaker than, a complete nonzero fiber law. originality.rationale: Accessible full primary texts were compared at statement/implication level: the q-to-one map and rank distribution from 2010, and fixed-initial-entry rank distribution from 2021, are strictly weaker than prescribed determinant fibers. Additional character-order Euler product and inversion are not in their inspected statements. Exact published-finding corpus searches and broad literature aliases gave no decisive equivalent or dominating result. Residual historical-access risks remain, and failed search is not proof of novelty.
residual_risks: Full text of Daykin (1960) not inspected; its known rank theorem does not rule out other determinant-counting material.
Full text of Cohen (1972) and Ballico–Elia (2014) not inspected; accessible descriptions suggest different invariants, so no definitive NOT_COVERING assessment of those whole papers.
Literature searches and indexed records are incomplete; equivalent resultant-character distributions in unlocated specialist sources remain possible.

value.rationale: Determines every value fiber of a natural determinant map, with explicit Ramanujan sums and all-order character spectrum. The sharp gcd(n,q-1)=1 boundary for nonzero-value equidistribution and the nonuniform arithmetic biases are structurally meaningful beyond rank totals; they encode new natural number-theoretic information without arbitrary parameter slicing.
